t: Among the following acid which has the lowest pKₐ value ?
s: Formic acid has no electron-releasing alkyl group, so its conjugate base is most stable; it is the strongest acid (pKa 3.75), i.e. lowest pKa.

t: Amongst the following the most basic compound is
s: In benzylamine the lone pair is localised on an sp³ N not conjugated with the ring. In aniline it is delocalised; in p-nitroaniline and acetanilide it is withdrawn even more.

t: Which one of the following is the strongest base in aqueous solution?
s: In water the 2° amine is the strongest base (balance of +I effect and solvation of the conjugate acid): (CH₃)₂NH>CH₃NH₂>(CH₃)₃N>PhNH₂.

t: The strongest acid amongst the following compounds is
s: The –I effect of Cl falls rapidly with distance. 2-Chlorobutanoic acid has Cl on the α-carbon, so it is the strongest acid (pKa ≈ 2.9), stronger than HCOOH (3.75).

t: Identify the compound that exhibits tautomerism.
s: 2-Pentanone has α-hydrogens and shows keto–enol tautomerism. 2-Butene and lactic acid have no such system. For phenol the keto form is negligible (aromaticity), and the expected answer is 2-pentanone.

t: The correct order of acid strength of the following compounds:
s: p-NO₂ (–R, –I) > m-NO₂ (–I only) > H > p-CH₃ (+I, hyperconjugation). pKa: 7.1 < 8.4 < 10.0 < 10.3.

t: Considering the basic strength of amines in aqueous solution, which one has the smallest pK_b value?
s: The smallest pKb means the strongest base. In water, dimethylamine is the strongest (pKb 3.27).

t: Which of the following is the strongest acid ?
s: Picric acid has three NO₂ groups at o/p positions (–R and –I), which delocalise the phenoxide charge most. Its pKa is ≈ 0.4.

t: Which of the following is the strongest base ?
s: Ethane (pKa ≈ 50) is the weakest acid among HC≡CH (25), CH₂=CH₂ (44), NH₃ (38) and C₂H₆, so its conjugate base C₂H₅⁻ is the strongest.

t: Which of the following order is expected to be correct ?
s: Acidity: ClCH₂COOH (2.86) > CH₃COOH (4.76) > CH₃CH₂COOH (4.87). So the pKa values increase in that order.

t: Which of the following compounds is the most acidic ?
s: Three Cl atoms exert a strong –I effect, which stabilises the carboxylate; trichloroacetic acid has pKa ≈ 0.7.

t: Out of the four pKₐ values 3.75, 9.89, 15.54 and 19.30, the highest pKₐ value corresponds to
s: Formic acid ≈ 3.75, phenol ≈ 9.9, methanol ≈ 15.5, acetone (α-C–H) ≈ 19.3. The highest pKa belongs to acetone.

t: The weakest base among the following is
s: The conjugate base of the strongest acid is the weakest base. Benzenesulphonic acid (pKa ≈ –2.8) is far stronger than phenol or alcohols.

t: For CH₃COOH (i), HCOOH (ii), CH₂ClCOOH (iii) and PhCOOH (iv), the order of acidity is
s: pKa: acetic 4.76, benzoic 4.20, formic 3.75, chloroacetic 2.86. So (i) < (iv) < (ii) < (iii).

t: Identify the group in which the order of basicity is not correct ?
s: OH⁻ is a much stronger base than NH₃ (the conjugate acid H₂O, pKa 15.7, is weaker than NH₄⁺, 9.25). So order (3) is wrong.

t: As the base changes from RNH₂ to R₂NH, to R₃N the basicity (in aqueous solution)
s: In water, 2° amines are the most basic. With R = ethyl, the order is R₂NH>R₃N>RNH₂ (+I effect balanced against solvation and steric hindrance).

t: The most acidic of the following substances is
s: p-Nitrophenol (pKa 7.1) is more acidic than phenol (10), acetaldehyde (α-H ≈ 17) and aniline (N–H ≈ 30).

t: The correct order of acidity of the C-H proton is –
s: Acidity increases with s-character of the C–H carbon: sp (25) > sp² (44) > sp³ (50).

t: Salicylic acid is a stronger acid than p-hydroxybenzoic acid due to
s: In the salicylate ion the o-OH forms an intramolecular H-bond with COO⁻, which stabilises the anion. pKa of salicylic acid is 2.97, against 4.58 for p-hydroxybenzoic acid.

t: Keto and enol forms of a compound are related to each other as
s: Tautomers differ in the connectivity of an H atom (C–H vs O–H), so they are constitutional (structural) isomers in equilibrium, not resonance forms.

(I) CH₃COOH (II) ClCH₂COOH (III) O₂NCH₂COOH (IV) HOCH₂COOH

t: Acetone and propen-2-ol are
s: CH₃COCH₃⇌CH₂=C(OH)CH₃: the two forms differ only in the position of an H and the double bond (keto–enol tautomerism).

t: Which of the following does not have an active methylene group ?
s: An active methylene group is a CH₂ (or CH) next to strongly electron-withdrawing groups such as NO₂, C=O or CN. In ethylamine, NH₂ does not activate the CH₂.

t:

s: Y (cyclohex-2-ene-1,3-dione type keto form) and resorcinol X differ only in the positions of H atoms and π-bonds; they interconvert by keto–enol tautomerism (the aromatic enol X predominates).

t: In which pairs first compound is stronger acid than the second ?
s: Phthalic acid (pKa1 2.9) is stronger than terephthalic acid (3.5): the nearby second COOH has a stronger –I effect and the monoanion is H-bond stabilised. Adipic (4.4) < succinic (4.2), fumaric (3.0) < maleic (1.9), and benzoic acid < picric acid.

t: IUPAC name of C₆H₅−N(D)−CHO is
s: The compound is an amide of methanoic acid (HCONH₂ = methanamide). Its N carries a phenyl group and a D, so the name is N-deutero-N-phenylmethanamide.

t: In the organic compound C^(1)H₂=C^(2)H−C^(3)H₂−C^(4)H₂−C^(5)≡C^(6)H, the pair of hybridised orbitals involved in the formation of : C₂−C₃ bond is
s: C-2 is a doubly bonded carbon (sp²) and C-3 is saturated (sp³), so the C₂−C₃ σ bond is formed by sp²−sp³ overlap.

s: The triple bond must get the lower locant, so the name is 4-bromobut-1-yne. The other names are correct.

t:

t: A compound having straight chain of five carbon atoms has one ketone group and two methyl groups on different-different carbon atoms. The IUPAC name of the compound is
s: The ketone is the principal group, so it takes the suffix “-one”; prefixes like “oxo” in (1) and (3) are wrong. (4) has both methyls on the same carbon. (CH₃)₂CH−CO−CH(CH₃)₂ is 2,4-dimethylpentan-3-one.

t: The IUPAC name of CH₃−CH₂−N(CH₃)−CH₂−CH₃ is
s: The parent is ethanamine, and N carries an ethyl and a methyl group. Alphabetical order gives N-ethyl-N-methylethanamine.

CH₃−CH(Br)−CO−O−C₂H₅
s: The acid part is CH₃CH(Br)COO⁻, 2-bromopropanoate, and the alkyl part is ethyl: ethyl 2-bromopropanoate.

s: C₆H₅COOC₂H₅ and C₂H₅COOC₆H₅ are both C₉H₁₀O₂ esters. They differ only in the groups on either side of the –COO– functional group, so they are metamers.

t:
Which of the following pair of compounds is not functional isomers ?
 [[img:a2521d279a17]]
s: (1) Alcohol/ether (C₄H₁₀O), (2) cyclic alcohol/ketone (C₄H₈O) and (3) unsaturated alcohol/aldehyde (C₃H₆O) are functional isomers. (4) is two esters (C₄H₈O₂) that differ only in the alkyl groups, so they are metamers.

s: CH₃CH₂CH₂CDO (an aldehyde) and CH₃COCH(CH₃)D (a ketone) have the same molecular formula C₄H₇DO but different functional groups, so they are functional isomers.

t: Hybridisation of carbon atoms present in the smallest ester are
s: The smallest ester is methyl formate, HCOOCH₃. The carbonyl C is sp² and the CH₃ C is sp³.

t: Total number of structural isomers possible from molecular formula C₈H₁₈ that contain 7 carbons in the parent chain are
s: A 7-C chain with one methyl branch gives 2-, 3- and 4-methylheptane. A branch at C-1 would just lengthen the chain, and C-5 and C-6 repeat C-3 and C-2. So there are 3 isomers.

t: How many 1° amines are possible with molecular formula C₄H₁₁N (only structural isomers)
s: NH₂ on a C₄H₉ group gives butan-1-amine, butan-2-amine, 2-methylpropan-1-amine and 2-methylpropan-2-amine, so there are 4.

t: How many tertiary alcohols is/are possible with molecular formula C₅H₁₂O ?
s: Only (CH₃)₂C(OH)CH₂CH₃ (2-methylbutan-2-ol) has OH on a tertiary carbon, so the answer is 1.

t: Which of the following compounds has wrong IUPAC name: [AIEEE 2002]

s: Saturated monocarboxylic acids (and esters) are CₙH₂ₙO₂. Diketones and dialdehydes are CₙH₂ₙ₋₂O₂, and diols are CₙH₂ₙ₊₂O₂.

t: Which one of the following does not have sp² hybridized carbon? [AIEEE 2004]
s: In CH₃−C≡N the carbons are sp³ and sp. The other three compounds contain a C=O carbon, which is sp².

t: The correct decreasing order of priority for the functional groups of organic compounds in the IUPAC system of nomenclature is [AIEEE 2008]
s: The IUPAC priority order is carboxylic acid > sulphonic acid > (anhydride > ester > acid halide) > amide > nitrile > aldehyde > ketone.

t: The IUPAC name of neopentane is : [AIEEE 2009]
s: Neopentane is C(CH₃)₄, i.e. 2,2-dimethylpropane.

t: Aspirin is known as : [AIEEE 2012]
s: Aspirin is 2-acetoxybenzoic acid, i.e. acetylsalicylic acid.

t: Which of the following is a correct name for the compound C₆H₅−C₆H₁₁ (a benzene ring bonded to a cyclohexane ring) ? [NSEC 2000]
s: A benzene ring carrying a cyclohexyl substituent is cyclohexylbenzene. Biphenyl (phenylbenzene) would have two benzene rings.

t: A compound with no tertiary hydrogen is : [NSEC 2001]
s: (CH₃)₃C−CH₂CH₃ has only a quaternary carbon, CH₂ and CH₃ groups, so it has no H on a 3° carbon. Compounds (1) and (3) each contain a (CH₃)₂CH− tertiary H.

t: How many structural isomers can be obtained by the replacement of one hydrogen atom of propene with chlorine ? [NSEC 2001]
s: The structural isomers are 1-chloropropene, 2-chloropropene and 3-chloropropene, so there are 3 (cis/trans forms of 1-chloropropene are not counted as structural isomers).

t: The shape of 2-butene is : [NSEC 2001]
s: The two sp² carbons and the four atoms attached to them lie in one plane, so the C=C framework of 2-butene is planar.

t: The IUPAC name of CH₂=CHCN is : [NSEC 2001]
s: The nitrile carbon counts as C-1, giving a 3-C chain with C=C at 2: prop-2-enenitrile (2-propenenitrile).

t: The number of isomers of C₆H₁₄ is : [NSEC 2001]
s: The isomers are hexane, 2-methylpentane, 3-methylpentane, 2,2-dimethylbutane and 2,3-dimethylbutane, so there are 5.

t: The compound which represents an unsaturated hydrocarbon is : [NSEC 2002]
s: Only propene contains just C and H and has a multiple bond. The other two contain N or O, so they are not hydrocarbons.

t: The number of possible primary alcohols with the molecular formula C₄H₁₀O is : [NSEC 2002]
s: The primary alcohols are butan-1-ol and 2-methylpropan-1-ol, so there are 2.

t: The IUPAC name of HOCH₂CH=C(CH₃)₂ is [NSEC 2003]
s: The C bearing OH is C-1, so the double bond is at 2 and the methyl at 3: 3-methylbut-2-en-1-ol.

t: The compound 2-Chloro-3-methyl-1-butanol has the following formula [NSEC 2006]
s: The structure is HOCH₂(C1)–CHCl(C2)–CH(CH₃)(C3)–CH₃(C4), which is (CH₃)₂CH−CHCl−CH₂OH. Option (4) is 3-chloro-2-methylbutan-1-ol.

t: How many different alcohols (not including optical isomers) are possible with the molecular formula : C₄H₁₀O? [NSEC 2006]
s: The alcohols are butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, 2-methylpropan-1-ol and 2-methylpropan-2-ol, so there are 4.

t: The C–C–H bond angle in ethylene is : [NSEC 2007]
s: The carbons are sp² (trigonal planar), so the C–C–H angle is about 120° (≈121°).

t: How many sigma bonds and pi bonds are present in CH₂=C=CH₂ ? [NSEC 2007]
s: There are 4 C–H σ bonds and 2 C–C σ bonds, giving 6 σ. Each C=C contributes one π, giving 2 π.

t: The number of ether metamers represented by the molecular formula C₄H₁₀O is : [NSEC 2009]
s: The ethers are CH₃OCH₂CH₂CH₃, CH₃OCH(CH₃)₂ and C₂H₅OC₂H₅, so there are 3.

t: How many position isomers are possible for chlorophenol ?

t: How many carboxylic acid structure isomers are possible with C₅H₁₀O₂ ?
s: The acids are C₄H₉COOH with the four butyl groups: pentanoic, 2-methylbutanoic, 3-methylbutanoic and 2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid, so there are 4.

t: CH₃−O−CO−CH₃ (Me–O–CO–Me) and Et–O–CH=O are
s: Methyl acetate and ethyl formate are both C₃H₆O₂ esters. They differ only in the alkyl groups on either side of –COO–, so they are metamers.

t: Which of the following represent correct pair of homologous ? (one or more correct)
s: Homologues belong to the same functional class and differ by (CH₂)ₙ. (2) Two alcohols differing by 2CH₂ and (3) two methyl esters differing by CH₂ qualify. (1) pairs a phenol with an alcohol, and (4) pairs a 1° amine with a 2° amine.

t: How many alkynes isomers are formed with molecular formula C₄H₆ ?
s: The alkynes are but-1-yne and but-2-yne, so there are 2.

t: Stereoisomers have different
s: Stereoisomers have the same molecular and structural formula (constitution). They differ only in configuration, the arrangement of atoms in space.

t: Which can show the cis-trans isomerism
s: Cis-trans isomerism needs restricted rotation with two different groups on each doubly bonded carbon. Only ClCH=CHCl meets both conditions.

t: Which of the following compounds will not show geometrical isomerism
s: In (CH₃)₂C=CHCH₃, C-2 carries two identical CH₃ groups, so it cannot show geometrical isomerism. Azomethane (CH₃N=NCH₃) does show syn/anti isomerism.

t:

t: Chiral molecules are
s: A chiral molecule is one that cannot be superimposed on its mirror image.

s: In (C) the central carbon carries two identical CH₃ groups. The plane containing C, H and C₂H₅ is therefore a plane of symmetry, and the molecule is achiral. (A), (B) and (D) each have four different groups.

t: Stereoisomers which are not mirror image of each other, are called
s: Stereoisomers that are not mirror images of each other are called diastereomers.

t: The instrument which can be used to measure optical activity, i.e., specific rotation:
s: Optical rotation is measured with a polarimeter.

t: (+) tartaric acid has a specific rotation of +12 unit when measured in 12 cm polarimeter tube and 2g/ml concentration at given temperature and light. When it is diluted to half the concentration, length of tube and other parameters being same, then the specific rotation will be
s: Specific rotation [α]=α/(l c) is a characteristic constant. Halving c halves the observed α, but [α] stays +12.

t: Which of the following pair of isomers can not be separated by fractional crystallisation or fractional distillation:
s: Enantiomers have identical physical properties (m.p., b.p., solubility), so they cannot be separated by these methods. Diastereomers and structural isomers can.

t: Which of the following amine is optically active?
s: sec-Butylamine, CH₃CH₂CH(NH₂)CH₃, has a chiral carbon. In the amines the N centre inverts rapidly, so (3) cannot be resolved.

t: How many geometrical isomers are possible for the given compound? Ph−CH=CH−CH=CH−COOH
s: Both C=C bonds can be cis or trans, and the molecule is unsymmetrical, so there are 2²=4 isomers.

t: How many geometrical isomers are possible for the given compound? CH₃−CH=CH−CH=CH−CH=CH₂
s: The terminal =CH₂ bond cannot show geometrical isomerism. The other two C=C bonds can, so there are 2²=4 isomers.

t: Total number of stereoisomers of compound CH₃−CH(OH)−CH(Br)−CH₃ is
s: There are two different chiral centres and the molecule is unsymmetrical, so there are 2²=4 stereoisomers.

t: Total number of optically active stereoisomers of tartaric acid is
s: Tartaric acid has three stereoisomers: (+), (–) and meso. Only the (+) and (–) forms are optically active.

s: Conformations are the different arrangements produced by (nearly) free rotation about the C–C σ bond.

s: Angle strain is largest where the bond angle deviates most from 109°28′. In cyclopropane the angle is 60°, a deviation of 24°44′.

t: The minimum torsional strain developed in butane is at dihedral angle(s)
s: Torsional strain is minimum in the staggered conformations, at dihedral angles of 60°, 180° and 300°.

s: (A) is the anti-staggered form, with the CH₃ groups at 180°. It has the least torsional and steric strain, so it is the most stable.

t: In 2-Fluoroethanol which conformer will be most stable ?
s: In the gauche conformer the OH and F are close enough for intramolecular H-bonding (O–H···F), so it is the most stable.

t: The least stable conformation of cyclohexane is
s: The order of energy is half chair (the transition state, highest) > boat > twist boat > chair.

s: In the boat form the two flagpole H atoms on C-1 and C-4 point towards each other and repel. This is the flagpole interaction.

s: In the chair form all the C–C bonds are staggered. The boat form has eclipsed bonds (C2–C3, C5–C6) and the flagpole interaction.

t: Number of conformational isomers of ethane.
s: Rotation about the C–C bond is continuous, so ethane has infinitely many conformations; staggered and eclipsed are just the two extremes. Key says (2).

t:

 [[img:fa076b4ae4cb]]

t: Which of the following orders is true regarding the acidic nature of phenol ?
s: o-Nitrophenol (7.2) is more acidic than phenol (10.0), which is more acidic than o-cresol (10.3). So phenol > o-cresol, and o-cresol < o-nitrophenol.

 [[img:1ddbfcdb6044]]

t:
Choose the most appropriate pair of nitrogens that gets protonated in the following structures.
 [[img:68ab32be886c]]
s: In the amidine, protonation occurs at the sp² imino N-1, because the resulting cation is resonance-stabilised by N-2 (two equivalent forms). In the second compound, the ring tertiary amine N-4 is protonated (answer key choice).

t:
Indicate the correct order of acidity (first ionization) in the following dicarboxylic acids :
 [[img:653cc6de22e1]]
s: The –I effect of the second COOH group decreases with distance. Oxalic (pKa1 1.27) > malonic (2.83) > succinic (4.2) > glutaric (4.34): III > I > IV > II.

t: Which one of the following compounds can be deprotonated by OH⁻ fastest ?
s: Proton transfer from an O–H acid to OH⁻ is very fast (diffusion controlled), and the most acidic species reacts fastest. HCOOH has the lowest pKa; toluene and methylamine (pKa > 15.7) are essentially not deprotonated.

t:
The order of acidities of the H-atoms underlined in the following compounds is in the order –
 [[img:de4391026236]]
s: Cyclopentadiene (pKa 16, aromatic anion) > phenylacetylene (sp C–H, ≈ 23) > benzylic C–H of ethylbenzene (≈ 41) > vinylic C–H of styrene (≈ 44).

t:
The preferred sites of protonation in the following compounds are
 [[img:5edded4f6fc5]]
s: Amides protonate on the carbonyl O (1); the resulting cation is resonance-stabilised by N, whose own lone pair is delocalised. In 2-aminopyridine the ring N (3) is protonated (amidine-type resonance), not the delocalised NH₂.

t: Which of the following phenols is most soluble in aqueous sodium bicarbonate ?
s: Solubility in NaHCO₃ needs an acid stronger than H₂CO₃. Three CN groups at the o- and p-positions (–R, –I) make 2,4,6-tricyanophenol strongly acidic (pKa ≈ 1), like picric acid.

t: The order of basicity is: (I) Ph−CONH₂ (II) Ph−NH₂ (III) Ph−CH₂−NH₂ (IV) p-CH₃O−C₆H₄−NH₂
s: Benzylamine (lone pair not delocalised) is the strongest base. p-Anisidine (+R of OMe raises e-density on N) is more basic than aniline. The amide is the weakest (lone pair delocalised into C=O).

t:

 [[img:f69362a8b4bb]]

t:
The order of basicity of the following compounds is
 [[img:3b6ed71f7179]]
s: The order is cyclohexylamine (sp³ N, pKb ≈ 3.4) > imine (sp² N) > aniline (lone pair delocalised) > pyrrole. Pyrrole’s lone pair is part of the aromatic sextet, so it is practically non-basic.

t:
The most basic nitrogen in the following compound is
 [[img:6db4aa8576ee]]
s: N-I (pyrrole type) has its lone pair in the aromatic sextet. N-II and N-IV are amide nitrogens (lone pair delocalised onto C=O). N-III is a pyridine-type N with an sp² lone pair available for protonation, so it is the most basic.

t:

s: (a) enolises to an aromatic phenol (resorcinol), giving ~100% enol. (d) acetylacetone has ~80% enol (conjugation + intramolecular H-bond). (c) the enol of an enone is a conjugated dienol, so it is more enolised than (b), a simple ketone with negligible enol.

t:

 [[img:ad2a65b48c90]]

t:
Among the following reaction which favours forward reaction ?
 [[img:0a1a580925f5]]
s: An acid–base equilibrium favours formation of the weaker acid and the weaker base. In (C), CH₃CH₂⁻ (conjugate acid ethane, pKa 50) removes H from CH₃NH₂ (pKa ≈ 40) to give the weaker base CH₃NH⁻. The other equilibria lie to the left.

s: Only acids stronger than H₂CO₃ (pKa 6.4) react with NaHCO₃. These are 2,4-dinitrophenol (4.1), benzoic acid (4.2) and benzenesulphonic acid. m-Nitrophenol (8.4) does not react.

t: How many structurally isomeric carbonyl compounds are possible with molecular formula C₅H₁₀O.
s: There are 4 aldehydes (pentanal, 2-methylbutanal, 3-methylbutanal, 2,2-dimethylpropanal) and 3 ketones (pentan-2-one, pentan-3-one, 3-methylbutan-2-one), giving 7.

t: Which of the following IUPAC name(s) is/are incorrect : (one or more correct)
